sentences.text: The case of the prosecution in nutshell is that, investigation was proceeded against accused persons regarding complaint registered by Assistant Manager, Bajaj Finance, Adarsh Solanki who works as sales executive at Bajaj Finance and on 15-04- 2023 the accused Aniket forged documents of Sanjay without his consent and approved loan on Samsung LED TV.
On 02-07-2023 thereafter he approved another loan in the name of Sanjay S/o Motiram fraudulently and purchased LG LED TV.
On the same day he took another loan for purchasing Haier fridge.
On 15-07-2023 impersonated his father Pawan Patel and obtained loan for Haier LED TV.
Later on committed same fraud on various occasions on different dates by changing number, name, photos, date of birth and Adhar Card details of different persons.

When such incidents were unearthed offence U/s 420, 467, 468, 471 of the IPC was registered and co-accused was arrested and in his disclosure statement under section 27 of Evidence Act he stated that along with present applicants he had conspired and had got approved loan from Bajaj Finance and present applicants used to provide him cases instead of items on which loan was granted.

On such incident offence was registered against present applicants U/s. 420, 467,
468, 471 of the IPC in Crime No.211/2024 at P.S, Pithampur Sector -- 1, District - Dhar (M.P.)
4.
Learned counsel for the applicants submits that the applicants have been implicated in this case only on the basis of memorandum statement of co-accused.
There is no material to connect the present applicants and they have been falsely implicated in the present case.
The conclusion of trial may take time, therefore, they may be granted anticipatory bail.
5. On the other hand, learned Public Prosecutor for the respondent/State has opposed the anticipatory bail application.
The applicants are absconding since the date of registration of FIR.
Investigation is still pending and therefore, custodial interrogation may be required.

On such grounds, he prayed for its 3 MCRC-22792-2024 rejection.
6.

After hearing rival contentions and going through the impugned order, this Court finds that the role attributed to the applicants is only to the extent that they were a witness of the agreement and no other material is available against them.
Therefore, this Court finds that there is no need for custodial interrogation of the present applicants in the matter.

7 . Accordingly, without commenting on merits of the case, the instant application is allowed and it is directed that in the event of arrest, applicants be released on bail on furnishing personal bond in the sum of Rs.1,00,000/- (Rupees One Lakh)each with one surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the Arresting Officer (Investigating Officer).
8 . The applicants shall make himself available for interrogation by the Investigating Officer as and when required.

They shall further abide by the other conditions enumerated in sub-section (2) of Section 438 of Cr.P.C.
9.

This order will remain operative subject to compliance of the following conditions by the applicants:-
